titulo: The sourced base: every number with the literal excerpt
hero_alt: Screen with a long transcript and a highlighted excerpt being copied into a table.
lead: The base.md is the heart of the channel with a source. Every number that goes on screen goes in with who said it, the video, the date, and an excerpt copied from the transcript, unedited. A script checks each excerpt; if any is not there, the video is discarded. Here you build your own base and your own checker.
objetivo: build the base.md for a video in your niche, with a literal excerpt on each line, and check each excerpt against the transcript with a script.

aprende.t: From the video to the transcript, on your computer
The five columns of the base.md
What a literal excerpt is (and what it is not)

secoes.titulo: From the video to the checked line

nos.detalhe: A video from one of the 5 channels in your canais.md. Write down the YouTube id, the date, and the title: they go in the "Video" column and in the source on screen.

The radars download only the audio and transcribe it on your own computer (inemavox, Whisper large-v3). Any local transcriber works. The transcript.txt file is the proof for everything that comes after.

Columns: number used, who said it, video (exact id), date, and excerpt. The excerpt goes in straight quotes and is a literal copy of a continuous piece of the transcript, 6 to 30 words, without editing or joining pieces.
The script normalizes the text (lowercase, no accents, no punctuation) and looks for each excerpt inside the transcript of the cited video. An excerpt that is not there fails the whole base.

secoes.legenda: The check does not judge whether the number is true in the world: it guarantees that someone said exactly that, in the cited video. That is why everything is attributed ("according to him").

secoes.sub: Illustrative examples, from an invented transcript for the real estate niche.

texto: Copy straight from the transcript, just as it is, even if the speech is loose. Between 6 and 30 words, enough to prove the number.

exemplo.texto: "o aluguel médio aqui na região subiu doze por cento em um ano"

texto: Swapping words to make it sound nicer breaks the check. The script can't find it and the video is dropped.

exemplo.texto: "o valor médio do aluguel na região aumentou 12% no último ano"

texto: Joining the start of one sentence with the end of another creates a sentence nobody said.

exemplo.texto: "o aluguel médio subiu… e vai continuar subindo em dois mil e vinte e sete"

texto: Two or three words show up anywhere and don't show the context. Use at least 6.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""usage: python3 confere.py base.md transcript.txt
Is each quoted excerpt in the base found in the transcript? Exits 1 if any is missing."""
import re, sys, unicodedata

def n(s):  # lowercase, no accents, no punctuation
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", s.lower()).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9%]+", " ", s)).strip()

base = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()
tx = n(open(sys.argv[2], encoding="utf-8").read())
fora = 0
for trecho in re.findall(r'"([^"]{20,})"', base):
    ok = n(trecho) in tx
    fora += not ok
    print("OK  " if ok else "FORA", trecho[:70])
sys.exit(1 if fora else 0)

abas.html:
OK   average rent in the region rose twelve percent in a year
FORA the average rent value in the region increased 12% in the last year

A FORA line: fix it by copying again from the transcript. The checar.py in the radars does the same for each video cited.

The transcript and the base can differ in accents, commas, or capitalization without the meaning changing. Normalizing both sides avoids failing a line for no reason, and it still catches a swapped word or a pasted sentence.

secoes.sub: Each line of the base goes through the checker. Stop it in the middle and run it again.
tarefas: Line 1 · rent rose 12% in a year

msg.inicio: 5 lines in base.md. Click "Check the base".
msg.rodando: Checking: each excerpt is searched for in the transcript of the cited video.
msg.parou: Stopped. The middle line was left as checking. Run it again.
msg.retoma: Resumed: the line that was checking goes back to the queue; the ones already found are not redone.
msg.fimfalha: One line is not in the transcript. In the radar, this fails the base: the script goes back once, and if it fails again, the video is not made.

secoes.legenda: Illustrative simulation in the browser. The failing line is deliberate: its excerpt was "improved" and is no longer literal.

exercicios.titulo: E3 · The base with its source
exercicios.texto: Transcribe a video from one of your 5 channels and build the base.md with the number, who said it, video, date, and literal excerpt. Run confere.py.
exercicios.pronto: each line has the literal excerpt in quotes and confere.py prints only OK.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: You replaced "twelve percent" with "12%" in the base excerpt to make it cleaner. What happens in the check?
opcoes: The script converts it on its own.
It only fails if the number is wrong.
The excerpt is no longer literal and the check fails.
Nothing: the meaning is the same.
perguntas.explica: Normalization ignores accents, punctuation, and capitalization, but it does not swap a word for a numeral. An edited excerpt is no longer a literal copy.

opcoes: That the number is true in the real world.
That someone said exactly that, in the cited video.
That the video will go viral.
perguntas.explica: It proves attribution, not truth. That's why everything is reported ("according to him") and trust comes from the choice of channels (lesson 3).

perguntas.p: Which excerpt works for the base?
opcoes: Your own summary of what he meant.
The start of one sentence pasted onto the end of another.
One continuous stretch of 6 to 30 words, copied from the transcript.
perguntas.explica: Too short doesn't prove context; a summary and a paste-up are not literal.
